question: Is the OECD/COINr pipeline's ranking instability under recipe sampling (C4 FAIL in EXP-INTEL-35434771791: canonical recipe 58%/48% agreement, per-task recipe untested) a sample-size artifact of the truncated-first-20 locatable_sample — such that ranking stabilizes when more elements per definition are available — or is the instability structural, arising from how definition filtering and recipe sampling interact regardless of sample size?
hypothesis: The ranking instability is primarily a sample-size artifact. With only 20 elements per task and 5-8 matching a given definition, recipe sampling (which subsets roles with p=0.5) has too few matching elements to稳定ly capture the discriminative signal. When the effective element count per definition is increased (via bootstrap resampling simulating larger samples), ranking agreement will improve because each recipe iteration captures a more representative subset of the definition-matching elements. Specifically: (H1) canonical recipe ranking agreement for tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP will be ≥80% when estimated at effective sample size equivalent to the full locatable count (21-82 elements); (H2) ranking agreement will increase monotonically with effective sample size from 5 to 20 elements; (H3) per-task recipe ranking agreement will be ≥70% at effective sample size 20.
falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if ANY of: (F1) Ranking agreement for tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP under canonical recipe does NOT reach ≥80% when extrapolated to the maximum effective sample size (20 elements, the full truncated-first-20); (F2) Ranking agreement does NOT increase monotonically with effective sample size (5→10→15→20) for tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP under canonical recipe — specifically, the Spearman correlation between effective_n and ranking_agreement is < 0.6; (F3) Per-task recipe ranking agreement for tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP is < 70% at effective_n=20; (F4) ANY definition × recipe combination that achieves ≥80% ranking agreement at effective_n=20 loses ≥20 percentage points when moving from effective_n=20 to effective_n=5, AND the reverse (gaining ≥20pp from 5→20) does NOT occur for any other combination — demonstrating instability is non-monotonic and not attributable to sample size.

baselines.description: Parent canonical recipe ranking agreement: tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP 58% (116/200 iterations), tag_entropy × DEF-FORM-ONLY 48% (96/200 iterations). From audit VF1 recomputation on EXP-INTEL-35434771791. This is the instability to be explained.

Non-recipe pipeline ranking agreement: tag_entropy preserves listing > detail for both DEF-FULL-MAP and DEF-FORM-ONLY (100% agreement). form_fraction and total_area fail under DEF-FORM-ONLY. From result.json M7_ranking_agreement and audit recomputed_metrics.

Non-recipe pipeline eta2: tag_entropy × DEF-FORM-ONLY = 0.9996, tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP = 0.996, form_fraction × DEF-FORM-ONLY = 0.995, total_area × DEF-FORM-ONLY = 0.998. All well above 0.05 threshold (parent range 0.964-0.999). Pipeline preserves discrimination; the question is ranking stability.

positive_control.description: Direct (non-pipeline) computation of tag_entropy, form_fraction, and total_area eta2 on page_type reproduces eta2=1.0 on the truncated-first-20 locatable_sample, confirming the raw features retain perfect discrimination before any pipeline processing. Same as parent PC1.
positive_control.expected: All three features: eta2 >= 0.99, within-type std < 0.001, listing_mean/detail_mean/cart_mean within 0.001 of parent values (tag_entropy: 2.646/2.484/2.602; form_fraction: 0.85/0.95/0.95; total_area: 341k/589k/428k).

null_control.description: The normalized hierarchy-weighted density formula (sum(exp(-alpha*depth)*inForm) / total_weight) produces eta2 < 0.01 on page_type, reproducing the y-proxy degeneracy anchor. Same as parent NC1.
null_control.expected: Normalized hierarchy density: eta2 < 0.01, all page type means within 1% of each other.

measurement_validity: All computations use existing raw evidence from EXP-INTEL-34782350557 (sha256: da30bd059adb555409784a2fd41402d533b64a25c89aa710b77e686a94a155050). No new data collection required. No browser/network/model calls.
The 7 tasks (3 listing, 3 detail, 1 cart deduplicated to n=1) with truncated-first-20 locatable_sample are the input. Within-type template invariance is inherited.

OECD/COINr definitions use the SAME role mappings as prior experiments: DEF-FULL-MAP (a→link, input→textbox), DEF-FORM-ONLY (form roles only), ISOLATED-A-LINK (link only). ISOLATED-A-LINK expected degenerate zero; analysis focuses on DEF-FULL-MAP and DEF-FORM-ONLY.

Feature-weighted density = sum(feature_value(elem) for elem matching definition) / elements_with_bbox. This replaces element COUNT with feature VALUE sum while preserving definition filtering and normalization structure.

Subsample analysis: For each effective sample size n ∈ {5, 10, 15, 20}, use the first n elements from each task's locatable_sample (which is ordered by DOM position). Compute feature-weighted density, eta2, and ranking agreement at each n. This simulates the effect of having more elements per definition.

Bootstrap resampling for uncertainty: At each effective_n, perform B=1000 bootstrap resamples of tasks within each page_type (with replacement), compute ranking agreement per bootstrap, and report mean ± std. This quantifies sampling uncertainty in the ranking agreement estimate.

Recipe sampling at each effective_n: For canonical recipe (shared subset p=0.5) and per-task recipe (independent p=0.5 per task), perform 10 seeds × 1000 iterations at each effective_n. This replicates parent protocol at each sample size.

Metrics bounded to 7 tasks, 1 Magento site, 3 definitions (2 non-degenerate), 2 recipes, 3 features, 4 effective sample sizes. Cart n=1 within-type variance degenerate; comparison focuses on listing vs detail.

CRITICAL LIMITATION: The raw data contains only truncated-first-20 locatable elements per task (20 of 21-82 available). Full DOM testing would require re-collecting data from the Magento Docker container. This experiment tests whether the instability is sample-size-dependent within the available 20-element range. If the instability persists at n=20, full DOM testing (n=21-82) is still needed for a definitive answer, but the n=20 result would strongly suggest structural instability.
decision_rule:
Conjunctive:

C1_RAW_FEATURES_REPRODUCE: The positive control PC1 passes: all three direct features achieve eta2 >= 0.99 on page_type with within-type std < 0.001. PASS if all three pass; FAIL if any eta2 < 0.99.

C2_HIERARCHY_NORMALIZED_REPRODUCES: The null control NC1 passes: normalized hierarchy density eta2 < 0.01 on page_type. PASS if eta2 < 0.01; FAIL if eta2 >= 0.01.

C3_FEATURE_PIPELINE_ETA2_NONZERO: At least one feature-weighted density through the OECD/COINr pipeline (any definition × any recipe × any feature) at effective_n=20 achieves eta2 >= 0.05 on page_type. PASS if max(eta2) >= 0.05; FAIL if all eta2 < 0.05.

C4_NATURAL_RANKING_PRESERVED: At effective_n=20, for at least one feature, the non-recipe pipeline preserves the same ranking of page types as the direct feature across both DEF-FULL-MAP and DEF-FORM-ONLY. PASS if >= 1 feature preserves ranking for both definitions; FAIL otherwise.

C5_SAMPLE_SIZE_EFFECT: Ranking agreement for tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP under canonical recipe increases with effective sample size. Specifically: (a) Spearman correlation between effective_n ∈ {5,10,15,20} and ranking_agreement is >= 0.6; AND (b) ranking_agreement at effective_n=20 is >= ranking_agreement at effective_n=5 + 0.10 (at least 10 percentage points improvement). PASS if both (a) and (b) hold; FAIL if either fails.

C6_RANKING_STABILITY_AT_FULL: At effective_n=20, canonical recipe ranking agreement for tag_entropy × DEF-FULL-MAP is >= 80%. PASS if agreement >= 0.80; FAIL if < 0.80.

VERDICT RULES:
- If NOT C1: MEASUREMENT_INVALID — raw features don't reproduce, cannot anchor.
- If NOT C2: MEASUREMENT_INVALID — hierarchy anchor fails, cannot compare.
- If C1 AND C2 AND NOT C3: FALSIFIES — pipeline collapses ALL feature-based discrimination at full effective sample size. Density-based MIXED handling is not viable.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND NOT C4: MIXED — pipeline discriminates but does not preserve natural ranking at full effective sample size. Feature-weighted density is achievable but produces different rankings than direct features.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4 AND NOT C5: MIXED — ranking is preserved by non-recipe pipeline AND at effective_n=20, but sample size does NOT improve ranking stability. The instability under recipe sampling is structural, not sample-size-dependent. Product lane should use non-recipe density only.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4 AND C5 AND NOT C6: MIXED — sample size helps but doesn't fully resolve instability. Partial improvement; additional full-DOM testing needed.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4 AND C5 AND C6: SURVIVES — ranking instability was primarily sample-size artifact. Pipeline preserves natural ranking at effective_n=20 under canonical recipe. MIXED program is unblocked with feature-weighted density using canonical recipe.
product_consequence_positive: If C5 AND C6 PASS: Resolves the MIXED program bottleneck. The ranking instability under recipe sampling (C4 FAIL in parent) was a sample-size artifact of the truncated-first-20 sample. Feature-weighted density through OECD/COINr pipeline with canonical recipe achieves stable task-type ranking at effective_n=20. Product lane can pursue density-based MIXED handling using tag_entropy-weighted density with the existing definition×recipe framework. The 31x recipe material gap (EXP-INTEL-35264637598) becomes actionable.
product_consequence_negative: If C5 FAILS (sample size doesn't improve stability) or C6 FAILS (agreement <80% at n=20): The ranking instability is structural — definition filtering × recipe sampling inherently destabilizes rankings regardless of element count within the available sample range. Product lane must use non-recipe density only (which preserves ranking at 100% per B2) and accept the eta2 reduction from recipe sampling (0.92-0.74 for canonical, ~0.36 for per-task). Full DOM testing (n=21-82) is still warranted as a final check but the n=20 result would strongly suggest the structural interpretation.
estimated_cost: VERY LOW — offline computation on existing reconstructed data. No browser/network/model calls. Compute feature-weighted density for 3 features × 2 definitions (non-degenerate) × 4 effective_n × 7 tasks = 168 density values, plus recipe-sampled densities (2 recipes × 10 seeds × 1000 iterations × 2 definitions × 3 features × 4 effective_n = 480,000 density samples — computationally cheap), plus bootstrap resampling (1000 bootstraps × ranking agreement computation). Estimated < 5000 LLM tokens for analysis code and < 60 seconds compute.
expected_information_gain: HIGH — directly resolves the critical ambiguity from parent EXP-INTEL-35434771791 (MIXED verdict, C4 FAIL). Either outcome (sample-size artifact vs structural instability) changes a concrete product decision about MIXED handling strategy. If sample-size artifact: MIXED program unblocked, product lane can use recipe density. If structural: product lane must use non-recipe density, closing a costly design path. The subsampling analysis also provides extrapolation guidance for full-DOM testing if warranted.
